jobs.occupation: Financial Controller (EMEA), Accounting, Controlling and Compliance
jobs.description:
_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for a Financial Controller to join our office in Copenhagen.

__CIP Fund Solutions is a platform delivery company working for Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) and funds managed by CIP in providing complex fund management and investment services.

_**Team

**You will join a dynamic and collaborative finance team working across +250 investment vehicles in varying legal structures in 20 EMEA countries. The team consists of 10 skilled financial controllers based in London, Sheffield, Madrid, and Copenhagen, creating a diverse and international working environment. The role is based in our Copenhagen office.

We are responsible for financial reporting, accounting, and compliance for a broad portfolio of companies, and we collaborate closely with the investment teams and external advisors across the region. The team values accuracy, ownership, and clear communication, while maintaining a supportive and informal culture where collaboration and continuous learning is key.

**Role

**Reporting into the EMEA Vice President of accounting, Controlling and Compliance, you will develop and maintain our finance setup for the investment vehicles, while having oversight and controlling of the day-to-day accounting performed by third-party service providers. In so doing, you will be responsible for establishing, implementing and delivering best-in-class finance processes.

**Responsibilities will further include:

**

• Controlling accounts including balance sheet reconciliations, IC loans, dual bookkeeping systems reconciliation, etc.

• Oversight of the P2P process performed by third-party service providers, ensuring timely approval of invoices and payments including aligning cash calls

• Ensuring timely submission and payment of tax filings including VAT, CIT, WHT etc.

• Overseeing and improving external service provider quality

• Overseeing the setting up of new investment structures

• Support mergers and acquisitions

**You

**You have an MSc in Economics or Finance and minimum 3 years of full-time experience in audit, financial controlling, or consultancy from a Big4 firm. You are motivated by building best practices, improving finance deliverables and improving CIP fund returns through effective operational finance execution.

**We look for the following in a candidate:

**

• Comprehensive knowledge of accounting and controlling

• Advanced analytical skills and attention to detail

• Effective time management, with the ability to prioritize assignments and manage short deadlines

• Solid communication skills and ability to collaborate across functions

• Curious and self-driven

• Fluency in English, both spoken and written

• Knowledge of corporate finance

• Experience with Business Central is an advantage

• German language is in advantage

**The process

**Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

**CIP Fund Solutions’ commitment to diversity and inclusion

**CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.

A diverse workforce allows CIP Fund Solutions to achieve results through different approaches and solutions to task execution and problem solving. We want all our employees to have equal opportunities for personal growth and career opportunities regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

**CIP Fund Solutions

**CIP FS’ purpose is to enable CIP’s ambition to scale rapidly over the coming strategy-period - supporting our colleagues with professional and efficient financial, legal, tax and business operations through the cycle from fund formation and capital raising, to deploying investments into construction of large-scale greenfield renewable energy assets, as well as M&A.

For more information, please visit CIP Fund Solutions.

jobs.occupation: Senior Game Programmer (Multiplayer)
jobs.description:
Do you feel personally responsible when players rage quit over a bad connection? Do you enjoy creating the tech that prevents it? Great! Help us.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We’re building something unannounced, exciting, thoroughly goofy and built to be played together online. We’re now looking for a Senior Game Programmer (Multiplayer) to implement the tech that makes it all work. This new project is living in a different world from our WHAT THE? games, built by a growing team with a playbook of its own.

**Here’s What You’ll Do Day To Day

**

• Build and iterate on smooth, low-latency online play on top of an existing game tech infrastructure, in close collaboration with designers, artists, and other programmers

• Work hands-on in Unity using the multiplayer framework Coherence

• Focus on multiplayer as your technical domain, working within the patterns and architecture already in place, and doing it in a way that keeps the codebase easy for others to build on

• Contribute to end-to-end user-facing feature development

• Share knowledge and raise the multiplayer bar across the studio over time

**Must-haves

**

• You’ve worked on at least one online multiplayer game (ideally shipped)

• You have a strong understanding of multiplayer networking concepts (e.g. peer-to-peer, client/host models, synchronisation, lag compensation), and you can explain them clearly to non-experts

• You understand the tradeoffs between peer-to-peer and server-authoritative approaches (bandwidth, latency, security, scalability), and can choose the right model for the problem

• You enjoy mentoring, knowledge-sharing, and helping others level up

• You’re willing to work on macOS and get comfortable with Apple-related constraints/tech because you’ll be working in the Apple ecosystem

**Nice-to-haves

**

• Experience with multiplayer game design

• Experience working on complex projects in a team of 20-30 people

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**This project is something new, but our ways of working are the same. We’ve always believed that games are made by teams, not solo rockstars, and good ideas can come from anyone. What we also believe in:

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward.

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You’re up for experimentation, and at the same time you don’t get too precious when the experience tells you you’re wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**

• We don't offer relocation support or visa sponsorship for this role.

• We work a 37-hour work week with flexible hours.

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

• Pension plan and private health insurance.

• Endless amounts of coffee.

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn't always work out, but we always learn something.

jobs.description:
**WHY SPEKTR

**At spektr, we are on a mission to automate the world’s most complex compliance workflows through AI. Founded by the team behind HelloFlow (acquired by Trulioo), spektr is building the infrastructure and AI agents to run compliance at scale.

_Compliance, built like product.

_Financial services has changed enormously. Much of the technology behind compliance hasn’t. Teams still spend hours on manual checks, disconnected systems slow down launches, and entering a new market can mean rebuilding the same processes all over again.

We’re changing that. spektr gives regulated businesses one platform for onboarding, monitoring and investigations, with configurable workflows and AI agents that do the legwork. Product, Operations and Compliance can move together, with the control they need to grow.

It’s a huge opportunity in an industry that has moved slowly for too long. We’ve built a product we’re proud to put in front of the most demanding customers. Now we’re looking for people who want to help get it into their hands.

• $26M raised, including a $20M Series A led by NEA, with backing from Northzone, Seedcamp and PreSeed Ventures.

• Customers worth getting excited about. We work with businesses including Pleo, Trustly, Nexi and Santander. These are large accounts with complex problems, ambitious teams and plenty of room for us to make a difference.

• Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for an AI Engineer who is, first and foremost, a product builder. In this role, you won't just be running experiments in a notebook; you will own the end-to-end AI strategy and its direct impact on our customers.

In this role, you will own everything related to AI, LLMs, and intelligent automation.

This is a high-impact role in a fast-growing company. We are looking for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves solving complex compliance puzzles, and is eager to shape the next generation of compliance technology.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

• AI Strategy & Ownership: Own the end-to-end AI roadmap—from selecting the right models (SOTA commercial vs. fine-tuned open source) to deciding how they are integrated into the product core.

• Agentic Feature Design: Design and deploy LLM-powered features including autonomous agents, advanced RAG pipelines, and intelligent document understanding.

• Product-Led AI: Collaborate directly with founders to translate complex compliance "puzzles" into scalable AI solutions. You own the "Why" behind every model choice.

• Continuous Innovation: Stay at the bleeding edge of AI/ML research, proactively identifying new papers or releases that can give spektr a competitive advantage.

• Engineering for Reliability: Turn non-deterministic AI outputs into deterministic product value. You ensure our agents are accurate, explainable, and hallucination-free.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• The Product Mindset: You are a product person at heart. You care about whether the AI actually solves the user's problem, not just if the loss curve is going down.

• High-Agency Builder: You prefer building systems over following manuals. You identify bottlenecks in our AI workflows and fix them before they become tickets.

• AI/ML Expertise: 2+ years of experience in ML, AI, or Data/Backend roles with a deep understanding of modern LLM stacks.

• Technical Mastery: Strong skills in TypeScript (our core) and/or Python, with hands-on experience in frameworks like LangChain or equivalent orchestration layers.

• RAG & Vector Mastery: You’ve built production-grade RAG pipelines and understand the nuances of embedding, retrieval strategy, and re-ranking.

• Evaluation Obsession: You understand that "it works on my machine" doesn't apply to LLMs. You have experience setting up evaluation frameworks to measure and improve model performance.

• Cloud & Scale: Experience deploying AI services in AWS or containerized environments, ensuring they are scalable and cost-effective.

• Communication: You can explain the trade-offs of a specific model architecture to a founder and a technical bottleneck to a peer with equal clarity.

**OUR TECH INTERESTS

**

• Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Open Source (LLaMA, Mistral).

• Stack: TypeScript, Python, LangChain, etc

• Infra: AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD for LLMs.

**OUR PROCESS

**

• Intro call with our Talent team (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (60 minutes)

**How To Apply

**We hire the smartest, kindest, and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work. You’ll be joining a team with a proven track record and the "Product-Market Fit" to change an entire industry.

**ORDERYOYO

****Lead Software Engineer – Payments

**Remote - **_Must be Copenhagen based

_**

• Quarterly team gatherings in one of our global offices

• Competitive salary

**About The Role

**At OrderYOYO, payments sit at the heart of everything we do. Every order placed, every restaurant paid, and every dispute resolved runs through the systems this team owns and operates.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer – Payments to help us build a more resilient, scalable, and compliant payments operating model — across online ordering and in-store platforms (POS, Kiosk, and payment terminals).

You'll play a central role in shaping how OrderYOYO handles money — from authorisation and settlement to disputes and merchant invoicing — across a rapidly growing, international restaurant platform.

****Role Mission

****Own and evolve OrderYOYO's payments capabilities — enabling KYC onboarding, deductions, settlement/payout timing, dispute flows, and merchant invoicing — while raising the bar on reliability, security, and engineering quality in one of our most business-critical domains.

****Core Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate payment-domain services, including gateway integrations and payment intent/authorisation/capture/refund flows, payout orchestration, and reconciliation.

• Implement marketplace capabilities where relevant: onboarding/KYC integration, merchant configuration, settlement instructions, deductions, and invoicing/merchant-statement alignment.

• Build robust “flow-of-funds” primitives — idempotency, ledgers/events, and audit trails — that are fully supportable for finance and compliance.

• Integrate with PSP and partner tooling, with close attention to tri-party / sub-merchant implications where applicable.

• Implement dispute/chargeback and fraud-handling touchpoints across internal workflows and PSP tooling, and collaborate with Ops on runbooks and escalation paths.

**

• Strong backend engineering background in distributed systems — microservices, async processing, resilient APIs, and eventual consistency.

• Production experience with payment flows (auth/capture/refund, webhooks, reconciliation) and “money correctness” patterns such as idempotency keys, double-entry thinking, and auditability.

• A solid security mindset: PCI compliance, PII protection, secrets management, least privilege, and secure coding practices.

• Clear, confident communication with non-technical stakeholders in high-stakes scenarios — incidents, financial breaks, and compliance requests.

**

• Experience with sub-merchant, marketplace, or Payfac-like operating models (KYC, underwriting, settlements, fee deductions).

**Who We Are

**At OrderYOYO, company culture comes first. We create a positive, inclusive environment where people are trusted to do their best work and take ownership of what they build. Personal development is central to how we work — engineers are encouraged to grow technically, take responsibility, and help shape how our products and platforms evolve.

We help restaurants succeed online by providing branded websites, mobile apps, and tailored marketing solutions, giving them full control of their business. By removing high commission fees charged by third-party platforms, we empower restaurants to grow sustainably.

Through our partnership with AppSmart, the market leader in POS and in-store systems, we've become the largest restaurant-focused platform in Europe.

**What We Offer

**

• A salary of DKK66,000/ month

• A role based in Copenhagen.

• High ownership and autonomy over the services you build.

• The opportunity to work on revenue-critical production systems.

• A strong focus on security, reliability, and engineering best practices.

• Real emphasis on learning, mentoring, and personal development.

jobs.description:
Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insight they need to make better financial decisions. All connected directly to the Danish tax authority. We're an independent company of around 65 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

We're looking for a Head of IT who wants to build something most companies are still only talking about: AI-native IT operations. You'll own our IT function end-to-end, with the mandate, the tools, and the backing to automate as much as you can. If automating IT operations excites you, and you want room to see how far it can go, this is for you.

What you'll build

Most IT functions run on people working through admin consoles and ticket queues. We want ours to run on systems: agents, pipelines and automations that do the work, with you as their architect. Often that means connecting systems yourself: using AI to integrate one tool with another, in a way that's secure and keeps personal data where it belongs.

A few pictures of where this could lead. Which become real, and how, is your call:

- Your team is the agents you build. They handle onboarding, access, devices and support. You decide what they do alone, what needs a human, and how that changes as they earn trust.

- IT you just ask. "Maria starts Monday as a data analyst" becomes an identity, licences, groups, an enrolled laptop and Slack access. Within policy, fully logged, and nobody opened an admin console.

- No standing access for people or agents. Access is granted when it's needed, justified, logged and removed automatically. Least privilege maintains itself instead of waiting for a quarterly review.

- Every agent is governed like a colleague. AI is spreading across every team here. Each agent, in engineering and beyond, gets an identity, a scope and a lifecycle, managed as rigorously as people.

What makes this hard is also what makes it worth doing. Our users trust us with their tax and financial data, and that trust is the business. So security and privacy aren't a layer on top of this work; they're the design brief.

An agent with admin rights is a new attack surface, so its permissions must be scoped, time-bound, auditable and visible to our 24/7 security monitoring. AI must never become a path for personal data to leave our control: what a model sees, where it runs and what it retains are decisions you make and defend. And when an agent is unsure, it stops and asks a human.

We plan to grow from 65 to 100+ people over the next few years, and IT has to keep pace. Automation has helped IT scale for years, but AI changes how much of the work it can take on. That combination, not hiring, is the main lever we want to use.

What you'll own

You'll own IT end-to-end:

- Identity and access: provisioning, access rights, least privilege and licence management

- Endpoints: a fleet of mostly MacBooks, with some Windows, managed via MDM.

- Hardware: laptops, screens, peripherals and meeting-room equipment, from buying and setting up workstations for new joiners to fixing what breaks

- Network: firewall, switches and access points

- Security controls: turning security requirements into practical configurations, and supporting our compliance work

- Day-to-day operations: onboarding, offboarding, Microsoft 365, Slack and hands-on support. When a laptop won't charge, or a VPN acts up, you're the person people turn to.

- Documentation and vendors: so things don't live only in your head, and so agents have the context they need

Beyond IT itself, every team here uses AI, and agents need identities, scoped access, managed devices and the right knowledge to work with. You'll work closely with our DevOps platform team on how engineers work with agents. You'll also help define how AI is set up across the company, including how agents get the context they need without seeing more than the person they act for.

How you'll work

This is a hands-on role with real ownership. You'll make the plans, set the priorities, weigh the trade-offs, and then do the work.

The big platform choices are made at company level. We're Microsoft-centred: hosting is moving to Azure, and Entra ID is our identity provider. One stack gives us one identity plane and one automation surface, all visible to our security monitoring. If you have good arguments for doing something differently, we want to hear them. Everything below that is yours: the tools, the vendors, the priorities and how it's built.

You'll report to our CTO. He won't manage IT; you will, and he's your sparring partner on direction. You'll own the IT budget, and decisions here are fast: if a tool will help, a lean procurement process gets it in place without committees.

You'll work directly with our Head of Security & Privacy, Legal Counsel, Engineering and the rest of the business, with no one brokering it for you.

Where you'll start

You'll take ownership of a recently insourced IT function, with the opportunity to shape its foundations. You'll assess what's there and decide what to keep, change or improve, so the foundations everything else builds on are yours.

From there, the arc is roughly this:

1. Solid foundations: make the setup yours, and strong enough to build on.

2. Automate the everyday: support, onboarding and access are the first and most obvious targets.

3. Scale: agents across the company, and IT that keeps up with growth by building first.

Who we're looking for

We're open to the exact background. What matters most is how you work: you think AI-first, you have a solid IT foundation, and you use AI to go deep on whatever comes next, with the judgment to know when its answers are right.

Must-have

- You think AI-first. You use AI in your daily work and reach for it first. You've built automations or integrations with AI, ideally ones that use AI themselves, and you can show us examples.

- You learn with AI, and judge what it gives you. When you meet a technology you don't know, you use AI to get up to speed, and you know enough to tell when its suggestion is right, wrong or risky.

- Automation excites you. You see a repeated task as something to automate, and you enjoy finding out how far automation and AI can take IT.

- Solid hands-on IT experience across infrastructure, endpoints, identity and security, including working knowledge of Microsoft Entra, Intune and Microsoft 365, and of managing MacBook fleets alongside Windows.

- Solid networking skills: You can design, run, secure and monitor an office network: firewalls, switches and Wi-Fi.

- Experience somewhere security isn't an afterthought. Finance or fintech is a good example.

- A security mindset that knows when to push back and when to keep things simple. You find solutions that protect without getting in people's way.

- Comfortable with hands-on end-user support. When someone's laptop isn't charging or their VPN is playing up, you're the person they turn to. You don't consider it beneath you, and you're good at it, even while you work to make most of it disappear.

Nice-to-have

- A software engineering mindset: you treat configuration as code, use version control and review changes before they ship

- Familiarity with security frameworks such as ISO 27001

Why join us

- Define what AI-native IT looks like. Few companies have figured it out yet. You'll get to figure it out here, with full ownership and room to experiment.

- AI without a meter. The best AI models for the job, like everyone here, with no cap on token spend. We care about using tokens well, not about limiting them.

- A product that matters. More than one million Danes use what we build to understand their finances.

- Small and solid. Independent and profitable, with no VC pressure and no layers between a decision and its outcome.

- Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal and genuinely collaborative.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone. We want to be upfront about this so you know what to expect.

And if we're asking people to be in the office, we want it to be worth their while. We're a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen, stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks, and lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street, proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

Reporting to: CTO

Start date: As soon as possible, ideally December 1st

jobs.occupation: Academic Employee in Coordinated Robotic Shipbuilding
jobs.description:
SDU Center for Large Structure Production (LSP), part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a fully funded position as Academic Employee in the area of model- and simulation-based planning and control of robotic shipbuilding operations (such as hull welding). The position will be vacant from 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter for a 3-year period – with the possibility of extension. Main work location is Odense/Denmark at SDU and Odense Havn (Odense Port).

Research environment

The candidate will be part of SDU’s newly established Center for Large Structure Production (LSP). LSP’s central ambition is to provide a physical “go-to” lab for companies in the sectors maritime, construction and energy to carry out research, development and testing of novel solutions in the production of large structures, such as buildings, ships and offshore platforms. In this context, the candidate is expected to work closely with our industrial partners on application-oriented use cases, while helping to commission and operate the unique set of equipment of the center. 

LSP is closely working together the companies at Odense Havn and similar partners making large structures across Denmark and Europe. LSP is integrated with the Odense Robotics Cluster involving startups and established companies in robotics. We are a team of currently 17 researchers and engineers, specializing in robot solutions involving modelling, simulation, and control of advanced robot technologies (systems and services) for application-oriented industrial applications. 

Our group is involved in a variety of national and European projects and features a strong network of academic and industrial partners. We solve challenging research problems derived from real-life challenges by implementing novel robot solutions. We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team, with flexible work organization and support of individual development.

Job description

The position as Academic Employee is associated with projects in the sectors maritime, construction and energy. The overall objective of the project is to develop, control and demonstrate LSP’s robotic solutions for executing central production operations, such as welding, 3D concrete printing and composite layup. The main activities in the projects will be industrial R&D tasks carried out by LSP’s engineers in close collaboration with company partners. 

The starting point for the candidate to develop their academic profile in LSP will be to work on so-called “zero programming” methods and tools to define a digital workflow from product design to production operations. Based on analyzing digital product descriptions, the candidate will develop detailed mode-, simulation, and data-based control strategies to carry out the required production operations, including multiple robots, tools, and sensors. Facilitating Digital Twins, these control strategies will then be further developed into control of the physical assets in LSP, i.e. its unique multi-purpose/multi-robot gantry system.

Profile and requirements

The candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:

• 
Documented education as engineer or technician

• 
Documented experience with simulation of industrial robots

• 
Strong programming skills (particularly in C/C++ and Python)

• 
Ability to work independently as part of an agile team, with a strong sense of responsibility

• 
Willingness to engage in application-oriented R&D, by closely interacting with company staff

In close teamwork with our researchers and staff from our industrial partners, the candidate will grow hands-on expertise in robotic production operations, including robots, tools, and sensors. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Head of Center, Professor Christian Schlette via email (chsch@mmmi.sdu.dk) or on LinkedIn (www.linkedin.com/in/christian-schlette/).

Application deadline: December 2, 2026 at 23:59 o'clock.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.”

Application must include cover letter, CV and certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

jobs.description:
The Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA), University of Southern Denmark (SDU, Campus Vejle), invites applications for PhD fellowships in Computer Science, with an emphasis on Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development.

We welcome applications from researchers interested in areas that include, but are not limited to:

• 
Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Developent, including approaches to improving the sustainability, efficiency, and reliability of software systems.

• 
Cloud and Distributed Computing, including cloud and edge computing, Internet of Things, microservices, serverless architectures, and web technologies.

The targeted starting period is Spring 2027, with room for flexibility.

Whom we are looking for

We are looking for motivated candidates interested in pursuing PhD research in Computer Science, particularly within the research areas relevant to SustainAI.

For the PhD position, applicants should possess, or be nearing completion of, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Processing Science, Advanced-Systems Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Ideal candidates demonstrate strong academic performance, research potential, and motivation to pursue scientific research.

Experience or demonstrated interest in empirical research methods, AI-driven software engineering, software architecture, formal methods, cloud-native systems, or software sustainability is particularly relevant. However, applicants with complementary expertise that can strengthen or expand SustainAI's research activities are equally encouraged to apply.

Fluency in English is required.

Candidates who have not yet completed their qualifying degree must obtain it before taking up the respective position.

Questions?

Curious to learn more about the positions, research topics, or working environment? Please feel free to contact Professor Valentina Lenarduzzi (lenarduzzi@imada.sdu.dk) for further information.

Hosting environment

The position will be part of the Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) located at SDU Vejle. 

SustainAI is a research group within the Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark's Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA). 

SustainAI conducts research at the intersection of software engineering, artificial intelligence, and sustainability, with the ambition of advancing the development, operation, and evolution of intelligent, reliable, and sustainable software systems.

The group’s research encompasses empirical software engineering, software architecture, software quality, AI-driven software development, cloud-native technologies, and the application of emerging AI techniques to software engineering challenges.

SustainAI combines foundational and empirical research with practical applications, promoting collaboration with international academic partners, industry, and public organisations. Its activities aim to advance software engineering knowledge and practices while addressing emerging technological, environmental, and societal challenges.

The group is part of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence at Campus Vejle, offering opportunities for interdisciplinary research, international collaboration, and professional development.

More information about SustainAI can be found at https://sustainai.sdu.dk/. 

The Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA).

The section brings together research and education in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, programming languages, and software engineering. Its activities focus on developing intelligent, secure, reliable, and sustainable software systems, combining fundamental research with practical applications and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Research within ACP addresses topics such as AI-driven software development, software architecture and evolution, programming language technologies, formal methods, distributed computing, cybersecurity, software quality, and trustworthy AI.

The section promotes collaboration with industry, public organisations, and international research partners to address emerging technological and societal challenges. Through its research, teaching, and knowledge-transfer activities, ACP contributes to advancing the foundations and engineering practices of modern computing systems while educating the next generation of computer science professionals and researchers.

More information about the section is available at https://acp.sdu.dk/.

The section is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science which offers an inclusive and international working environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong traditions of collaboration across research groups, departments, and faculties, as well as with external organisations, including educational institutions, municipalities, and companies.

The degrees offered by the department include BSc and MSc degrees in Computer Science, a BSc degree in Artificial Intelligence, and an MSc degree in Data Science.

More information about the department can be found at https://imada.sdu.dk/.

The University of Southern Denmark (SDU) was founded in 1966 and has more than 27,000 students, almost 20% of whom are from abroad. The university has more than 3,800 employees and offers 115 study programmes across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering.

The positions are based at SDU Campus Vejle, part of the university's growing activities in computer science and artificial intelligence. Vejle provides an international and welcoming environment, combining an active urban centre with easy access to nature and recreational areas. Its central location in Denmark offers convenient connections to other major Danish cities and international transport hubs.

jobs.occupation: Head of Accounting
jobs.description:
Do you want to help shape the future of EV charging from the finance side? We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Head of Accounting to lead the accounting function at Spirii, a fast-growing e-mobility scale-up and part of the Edenred Group. The role ensures reliable financial records, a disciplined close and reporting process, statutory and VAT compliance, effective controls and a strong team. The business has complex accounting and international VAT requirements, and its processes, systems and controls continue to evolve as it scales.

• Accounting operations, month-end close and Group reporting

• Lead day-to-day accounting operations, including general ledger, Accounts Payable, bank accounting, fixed assets, accruals, prepayments, provisions and intercompany accounting, as applicable.

• Own monthly and annual close, ensuring accurate and timely transaction recording, cut-off, reconciliations, supporting documentation and resolution of outstanding items.

• Ensure Balance Sheet integrity and oversee local statutory financial statements under Danish accounting requirements; lead the external audit process and respond to audit requests.

• Prepare and submit the Balance Sheet reporting package to Group under IFRS every two months; coordinate queries with Group Finance and meet Group deadlines.

• Set up, maintain and enhance the ERP system with support of the ERP expert to ensure effective accounting and to enable relevant data for FP&A and the business.

• Internal controls, risk management and audit remediation

• Own the design, documentation, implementation and monitoring of controls across accounting and VAT processes, including segregation of duties, approval workflows, access rights and reconciliations.

• Identify control weaknesses, financial risks and recurring process failures; maintain clear procedures and evidence of control execution.

• Follow up findings from internal and external audits, control reviews and risk assessments; agree owners, actions and deadlines with process owners, monitor completion and escalate significant or overdue issues to the CFO.

• The role is responsible for the remediation of finance findings from internal audits, but not for the overall internal audit process.

• VAT and statutory compliance

• Oversee VAT accounting, returns, reconciliations and compliance in Denmark and other relevant jurisdictions, including international registrations and correct treatment of domestic and cross-border transactions.

• Ensure timely statutory filings for corporation tax, transfer pricing, tax payments, Danmarks Statistik declarations and other required legal registrations; coordinate with external tax advisers and local representatives as needed.

• Maintain supporting documentation and a robust VAT control framework; identify and address compliance risks, recurring errors and potential exposures.

• Cash management

• Monitor and report actual cash balances weekly and maintain a rolling short-term cash outlook covering expected receipts and payments. Explain material variances and flag potential cash shortfalls or significant payment commitments.

• Team leadership, stakeholder management and continuous improvement

• Lead, organise and develop a team of 4, setting clear responsibilities and objectives, managing workload and performance, and building technical capabilities.

• Partner with FP&A to ensure reliable accounting actuals and supporting information; coordinate with Group Finance on accounting policies and reporting requirements.

• Partner with the rest of our finance team to support timely and accurate billing and VAT compliance.

• Work with business stakeholders and IT to improve accounting processes, documentation, systems, automation, data quality and integrations; reduce manual work, errors and bottlenecks, and ensure changes are appropriately tested and controlled.

• Build effective relationships across Finance and the wider business, resolving issues that affect accounting, reporting and compliance.

**How The Role Fits In Finance

**You will own accounting operations, local statutory accounting, VAT compliance, internal controls, follow-up on audit findings and the Balance Sheet reporting to Group. You will work closely with FP&A, who own monthly P&L reporting, budgeting and forecasting, and with our billing team, who own billing calculations and controls.

**Candidate profile

**

• 10+ years of relevant experience in accounting, finance operations or financial control, including senior accounting leadership.

• Experience from an international group environment is required.

• Experience from EV or e-mobility, fintech or transaction-based businesses is a strong plus.

• Degree in Accounting, Finance, Auditing or a related field; professional accounting qualifications are an advantage.

• Strong knowledge of accounting, month-end close, Balance Sheet reconciliations, statutory accounting, financial controls and international VAT.

• Knowledge of Danish GAAP (Årsregnskabsloven) and IFRS.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central ERP is required.

• Fluent or native Danish and professional fluency in English are required.

• Proven ability to lead and develop a team, improve finance processes and controls, and work effectively with Finance, Group and business stakeholders; structured, analytical and hands-on.

**What Success Looks Like

**A reliable and timely close; accurate Balance Sheet reconciliations and on-time Group submissions; effective controls and prompt remediation of findings; robust VAT and statutory compliance; clear weekly cash visibility; and a capable, accountable team delivering continuous improvement.

**Benefits

**It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii Gym or join a Spirii Run with colleagues.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

**About Spirii – Who We Are

**Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.
